m.text.body: This room is intended for discussion, implementation, and MSC drafting of Presence v2 via Selective Presence. Selective Presence allows users to select which users they'd like their presence changes to be pushed to. This is done through UI elements allowing users to select a list of "friends" to share data with. Additionally, options such as room-wide defaults or DM based selection for who to trust by default. Their presence changes will be sent to only those users, reducing excessive network requests.

content.body:
This room is intended for discussion, implementation, and MSC drafting of Presence v2 via Selective Presence.

After https://matrix.to/#/!nD4Jy1hp0We0VmIM9ubjqWLBX_uV8YlTBBPa3a_v2uk/$pky9awpkMJUWeJPhTjcPaBZ7EPtAQ6rlKWUs9nCx66s, this room was created to promote discussion and help move forward the act of modernizing presence in the spec.

## Presence v2?

The following concepts for Presence v2 were discussed in that conversation, and I have given them the following names:
a. **Presence v1** (Push) - When a user goes online, an EDU is sent to every server that they share a room with, and these responses are sync'd to the users of those rooms. This is the current implementation, disabled on many homeservers. This introduces substantial write amplification: for 10000 servers and 50000 users, this is a worst case of 60k network requests (and often full TCP connections, barring HTTP2) sent. This isn't just on presence state changes: Synapse sends regular "heartbeat"-esque presence EDUs per online user to prevent them from triggering an offline timer.
b. **Socket Synced Presence** (Pull) - Servers keep long-lived persistent connections between each other to share presence data. Although this makes live data possible, it was rejected because it is very, very expensive and requires long-lived S2S connections, something intentionally not part of current Matrix.
c. **Polled Presence** (Pull) - Clients request specific users in view to them, and servers poll the origin homeservers regularly for presence changes. This is a feasible alternative to Selective Presence, and I would like to see investigation into this method as well, however this is out of scope for this room which specifically covers Selective Presence.
d. **Selective Presence** (Push) - Users opt-in for which other users they would like to see their presence data. Their homeserver pushes these changes to those specific servers - none more, none less. Inspired by Jabber/XMPP's current presence solution.

This room solely exists to discuss the Selective (push) Presence, as it is the best fit for the current Matrix federation model that I can see so far.

## Guiding Factors

* Opt-in presence solves many of the write amplification problems, while keeping presence usable for users who desire it.
* Presence should be incremental (see Cat's draft) and batched.
* "Rich" (live data) is technologically different from typical presence, though the line where they differ is unclear. Presence v2 may include rich presence, however that is out of scope for the first drafts. - Textual user statuses MAY be in scope, with this series of MSCs replacing [MSC4426](https://github.com/matrix-org/matrix-spec-proposals/pull/4426) if so.

## Prior Art

[Cat's draft "Incremental Heartbeat Assisted Presence," which these drafts build upon](https://github.com/FSG-Cat/matrix-spec-proposals/blob/FSG-Cat/Incremental-Heartbeat-Assisted-Presence/proposals/XXXX-incremental-heartbeat-assisted-presence.md)

[Federation EDU reconciliation](https://github.com/gamesguru/matrix-spec-proposals/blob/4e474f20c60b65e2da95cc4c9fbf7f74e6de8aac/proposals/0F02-federation-edu-reconciliation.md)

[XEP-0198: Stream Management](https://xmpp.org/extensions/xep-0198.html)

content.body:
## Current Concept

Selective Presence allows users to select which users they'd like their presence changes to be pushed to. This is done through UI elements allowing users to select a list of "friends" (terminology may change later) likely to be stored within an account data event. Additionally, options such as room-wide defaults or DM based selection for who to trust by default. Their presence changes will be sent to those servers as an EDU listing which users they are to be sync'd to.

An extension to Simplified Sliding Sync will be used ("Sliding Presence Sync") and introduced in an MSC to allow clients to share with the server which users' "presence dots" are actively in view. This reduces overall write amplification of even selectively chosen presence - as the client is only receiving updates for clients actively in view. These two decisions together drastically reduce network requests sent for presence streams.

Additionally, to remove Synapse's unspecified presence heartbeat behavior, something similar to Cat's draft above will be implemented to allow presence states to realize if the users' server is online/offline. This will likely be its own MSC.

## Components

* MSCXXXX: Server-to-server heartbeats
* MSCXXXX: Sliding Presence Sync (depends on [MSC4186](https://github.com/matrix-org/matrix-spec-proposals/pull/4426))
* MSCXXXX: Presence v2 via Selective Presence

## Open Concerns

* Are S2S keepalives something useful to other areas of the spec? How might these actually look?
* What are the rules for when presence is sent to another user?
* Feedback from client/homeserver developers as to how this might actually look in reality
* Writing of drafts for all 3 MSCs
* How Rich Presence is related to these proposals (out of scope? handled by a similar mechanism in a future MSC?)
* If User Status Profile Fields are in scope for this MSC

content.body:
the current gist of our proposal is:
- specific specification of batching behavior, especially for s2s EDUs and sync responses
- extension of presence TTLs to be far longer than Synapse's current ~30 seconds (a lot of the expensive part seems to be the "x is still online" not the state transitions)
- potentially using something like Cat's draft for Incremental Heartbeat Assisted Presence (as pinned) to use server "online indicators" (like recent receipt of a transaction, or the federation send backoff) to make presence potentially even _permanent_ until a server is seen as "down"
- potentially a sliding sync extension or something adjacent to prevent the write amplification caused by presence changes in large rooms (think about it - my server knows 10k destinations and 30-40k users...  in the worst case, that's 9999 EDUs sure, but also... 40k sync responses to people who don't even care about me!)

and then, of course, Selective Presence:
- an account_data event to list users and rooms to share presence EDUs with, alongside a room state event m.room.presence_sharing to act as a "default behavior" _hint_ for small rooms or DMs
